title: Modernizing Government Travel Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on January 10, 2017. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Modernizing Government Travel Act

(Sec. 2) This bill requires the General Services Administration (GSA) to prescribe regulations to provide for the reimbursement of federal employees traveling on official business for the use of a transportation network company (e.g., Uber or Lyft) or an innovative mobility technology. The Administrative Office of the United States Courts shall prescribe such regulations with respect to judicial branch employees.

An "innovative mobility technology company" is an entity that applies technology to expand and enhance available transportation choices, better manages demand for transportation services, or provides alternatives to driving alone.

A "transportation network company" is an entity that uses a digital network to connect riders to drivers in order for a driver to transport the rider to a point chosen by the rider. This does not include a shared-expense carpool or vanpool arrangement that is not intended to generate profit for the driver.

(Sec. 3) The bill revises the reporting requirements regarding payments pertaining to official travel.

Each agency must annually submit to the GSA data on agency payments for travel and relocation and an analysis of transportation costs.

The GSA shall make the data submitted publicly available upon receipt.

The GSA shall annually submit to the Office of Management and Budget and to specified congressional committees an analysis of the data submitted for specified agencies and a description of any new regulations or changes to existing regulations.

summary.headline: This law lets federal employees be reimbursed for rideshare and similar transportation when traveling on official business, and requires agencies to report travel payment data.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs the General Services Administration to write rules that allow federal employees traveling for work to be repaid for using ride services like Uber or Lyft, or other innovative mobility options. The Administrative Office of the United States Courts must write similar rules for judicial branch employees. It also requires each agency to send the GSA yearly data on travel and relocation payments and a review of transportation costs, and the GSA must make that data public when it receives it.

who_it_affects.group: Federal executive branch employees who travel for official business
who_it_affects.how: They may be reimbursed for rideshare or other transportation network company trips taken while on work travel, under the rules GSA issues.

who_it_affects.group: Federal judicial branch employees who travel for official business
who_it_affects.how: The Administrative Office of the United States Courts must issue rules allowing reimbursement for similar ride services during work travel.

who_it_affects.group: Rideshare and transportation network companies such as Uber and Lyft
who_it_affects.how: Their services become eligible for reimbursement when used by federal travelers, under the new regulations.
Each agency must submit annual travel and relocation payment data and a transportation cost analysis to the GSA.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the public interested in federal spending
who_it_affects.how: The GSA must publish the agency travel payment data it receives, making it available to view.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law does not list a specific effective date; it depends on when GSA and the courts issue their implementing regulations and when the annual reporting cycle begins.
